'''''Odontoschisma sphagni''''', commonly known as '''bog-moss flapwort''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Odontoschisma sphagni |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Odontoschisma-sphagni.pdf |website=www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk}}</ref> is a species of [[liverwort]] in the family [[Cephaloziaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gradstein |first=Robbert |last2=Ilkiu-Borges |first2=Anna Luiza |date=October 2014 |title=A taxonomic revision of the genus Odontoschisma (Marchantiophyta: Cephaloziaceae) |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/S-Gradstein/publication/272363293_Taxonomic_monograph_of_the_genus_Odontoschisma_Cephaloziaceae_based_on_molecular_and_morphological_evidence/links/59a00522a6fdcce2df63db5c/Taxonomic-monograph-of-the-genus-Odontoschisma-Cephaloziaceae-based-on-molecular-and-morphological-evidence.pdf |journal=Nova Hedwigia |pages=17-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Odontoschisma sphagni (Dicks.) Dumort. |url=https://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0001196594 |website=www.worldfloraonline.org}}</ref> It grows in raised [[bogs]] on moist, [[Peat|peaty]] soil, on rotten and dead wood or on thin soil covering moist sandstone rock in [[evergreen]] or [[deciduous]] forests. It sometimes grows among mosses.<ref name=":0" />

== Description ==
it is a [[Prostrate shrub|prostrate]] plant, meaning it grows horizontally rather than upwards; in large, dense mats.<ref name=":0" /> Pale yellow-green to reddish-brown in colour. Leafy shoots are between 1-5 cm long and 1.2-3 mm wide, usually not branched. The stem is colourless and rigid; 10-15 cells tall, made of 60-120 [[epidermis]] cells around 70-100 larger inner cells. Undivided flat leaves, 0.9-1.4 mm long, and cylindrical perianths. [[Spore|Spores]] are 10-15 μm in diameter. Gemmae absent.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==
''O. sphagni'' is found in temperate-suboceanic areas of [[Europe]] and [[North America]], as well northern [[Mexico]]. It grows at low elevations, up to 1,500 meters in Jamaica. In Europe, it is found in Poland, western Russia, Bulgaria, northern Italy and Spain, Madeira and the Azores.<ref name=":0" />
[[File:Odontoschisma sphagni microscope.jpg|thumb|Under a microscope.]]
In the [[New World]], ''O. sphagni'' was originally described as ''O.'' ''prostratum''. Compared to Europe, ''O. sphagni'' in the Americas is slightly smaller, and prefer to grow on soil or soils over rock.<ref name=":0" />
